boundary.resolution: Twelve installed base globals, actual primitive aliases versus ordinary BIOS closures, language values and ordinary globals; CPU/Memory/protected-calls/SYSTEM own connected contracts. No new MMIO unit or complete BIOS/library/loader claim.

registers.resolution: All12 actual source interfaces, argument kinds, optional/missing nil distinctions, exact results/counts/errors and mutable dependencies. These functions introduce no additional mapped register bank; SYSTEM owns diagnostic ports.

datapath.resolution: Assertion tuples/original errors, equality/type/text categories, complete numeral grammar and ordered Number arithmetic, iterator factories and ordinary inherited reads, raw next storage, select word conversion/suffix and live global identity.

visibility.resolution: Direct API effects, iterator construction versus stepping, failed operation after already-written global value, print codepoint output versus separate byte history and flush; no rollback or drawing/presentation promise.

timing.resolution: Five primitive aliases add1 builtin cycle with zero argument/result coefficients; ordinary wrappers and digit/exponent/scanning/conversion/console work are not a fixed service time. Extremely large exponents carry no termination bound.

interrupts.resolution: Ordinary CPU/IRQ delivery and protected-call hardware-exception boundaries are supplied by their owner chapters. These base interfaces do not provide IRQ setup, acknowledgement or an IRQ-wait replacement; SYSTEM owns diagnostic transport.

faults.resolution: Exact wrapper error Strings, arbitrary/nil assertion payloads, alias argument errors and delayed iterator indexing/call faults; actual protected calls and SYSTEM fault publication supply connected routes. No generic all-failure recovery promise.

reset.resolution: BIOS main/base startup installs these public bindings; Memory supplies typed program storage/initialization and CPU/SYSTEM supply reset. No independent API register reset words or universal ordinary-global/history clearing promise is introduced.

programming.resolution: Short assertion, conversion, traversal and global-access examples accompany argument, returned-value and error reference.
